meta.title: Cuelith · Live projection software, lightweight and modular
meta.description: Cuelith puts lyrics, texts and announcements on the projector, the stage monitor and every other screen. Free and open source, it starts light and grows with the plugins you need.

hero.eyebrow: Live projection software · free and open source
hero.title: Live projection that starts light and grows with you.
hero.lead: Cuelith puts texts, lyrics and announcements on the projector, the stage monitor and every other screen. The core does a few things and does them well; you add the rest with plugins, only if you need it.
hero.shotAlt: The same text on three screens: the projector in the room, the Cuelith control view and the remote on a phone.

pillars.title: Three choices, taken all the way

items.title: Install only what you use
items.text: Out of the box, Cuelith is an essential tool: playlist, slides, preview, program and outputs. Songs, protocols and tools are plugins you switch on and off without restarting.

items.title: The screen stays on
items.text: Every plugin runs in its own separate space, with only the permissions it declares. If one stops responding, it is restarted automatically and the projection carries on. Your show is saved safely and recovered after a crash.

items.title: Free, with no surprises
items.text: The app is open source and needs no account. It works offline, and your shows, songs and images stay on your computer.

features.title: Built for the person at the desk, even working alone

rows.title: Always see what is on air and what comes next
rows.text: Playlist on the left, slides in the middle, program and preview on the right. One click prepares, one key goes live, with the fade you choose.
points: Five layouts: for presenting, for bands, for conferences
Keyboard shortcuts for everything: next, back, blackout, song sections
Program and preview swap sizes with one click; slide thumbnails grow so you can read the text
Search and go (Ctrl+K): plugins, commands, settings and playlist in one search
Timer and messages for the people on stage
rows.alt: Cuelith control view with playlist, slides, program and preview.

rows.title: One piece of content, a different screen for each audience
rows.text: Press “Next” once. The room gets large text over the background; the stage gets the text, the next slide, the clock and messages from the desk.
points: As many outputs as your computer can connect
Blackout and freeze on a single output, leaving the others alone
Backgrounds per slide, per item or by default, animated ones (GIF) too, with a dim layer for legibility
Text styles you create, with outline and shadow: text shrinks instead of breaking its lines
"Background only": one click hides the text on the outputs and keeps the background
rows.alt: Two outputs with the same content: the room shows the text over a background, the stage shows the text with the next slide and the clock.

rows.title: Songs with sections, ready for a band that improvises
rows.text: Verse, Chorus and Bridge become large buttons: when the band goes back to the chorus, you are there in one tap. Songs import and export in the open OpenLyrics and ChordPro formats.
points: Libraries searchable by title, lyrics, author and number
Editor with a preview of what the audience sees, slide by slide
Projection order kept separate from the lyrics
Credits and authors always in place
rows.alt: Band layout: song sections as large buttons.

rows.title: As a team, with tablet and phone
rows.text: On the same network, a tablet becomes a second control desk and a phone becomes the speaker's remote. It opens in the browser, with nothing to install, and pairs with a code.
points: Different roles: operator, remote, view only
Works offline, on the venue network alone
Every device can be revoked with one click
rows.alt: The remote on a phone: slide on air, next slide, Back and Next.

rows.title: Know in advance whether the computer can cope
rows.text: An indicator shows how much the app and the active plugins use, at rest, now and at peak, compared with what your computer actually has.
points: Frames per second for every output
Usage for every plugin, declared and measured
One colour to watch: green, yellow, red
If the computer is about to run out of memory, Cuelith stops the heaviest plugin before everything falls over, and tells you
Measured: twelve plugins together take about 300 MB and use no processor while idle
rows.alt: Settings, Resources section: memory, processor and output frame rates.

items.title: Conferences and schools
items.text: A running order of talks, notes, a timer with time colours and messages to the speaker.

items.title: Concerts and bands
items.text: Sections as buttons, projection order, lyrics and next slide on stage.

items.title: Churches and communities
items.text: Songs with sections, announcements, texts and backgrounds. One monitor for the musicians and one for the speaker.

items.title: Live streaming and events
items.text: Camera, scenes, lower thirds and streaming will arrive as plugins, on the same app.

plugins.title: The core does little. You choose the rest.
plugins.lead: Every plugin installs from inside the app, declares what it can do before you switch it on, and can be turned off at any time. Some add a tool to the control view; others work in the background, like audio and video protocols. You find them in an instant with search (Ctrl+K), set them all up from the same window and, the first time you start, a guide suggests the most useful ones.

permissions.none: Asks for no permissions: no internet, no files
permissions.storage: Saves its data on your computer
permissions.native: Native program, with full access to the computer

plugins.soonNote: Coming plugins are planned, with no promised date. When they are released they appear here and in the app.

developers.title: Want to write one?
developers.text: The plugin system is open: anyone can add a tool, a protocol or a layout. The source code includes an example plugin to start from. Cuelith is free software, but your plugin is yours: you choose its licence, free or paid, open or closed.

plugins.marketplaceLink: See every plugin in the marketplace

download.title: Ready in two minutes
download.lead: Free, with no sign-up. Updates arrive on their own and install only when you decide, never while you are on air. The installer asks for your language; if Cuelith is already installed, it updates it and leaves your shows, settings and plugins where they are.
notes: Windows may ask for confirmation on first launch, because the app is new and does not have a paid signature yet: choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
You do not need to be an administrator of the computer.
8 GB of memory recommended. Integrated graphics are enough for text and images.

versions.title: All versions
versions.lead: Every version stays available, with its notes.
versions.empty: The list of versions is not available right now. The download above always gives you the latest one.

items.a: Yes. The app is open source and will stay free, along with everything you need to use it. Today all available plugins are free too; whoever writes a plugin may decide to sell it.

items.q: Who can use and modify the source code?
items.a: Anyone. Cuelith is free software under the GPL: you can study it, change it and share it. If you distribute a modified version, you must share its source code under the same licence, so Cuelith stays free for everyone. Plugins are separate programs: their authors choose their own licence. The name “Cuelith” and the logo remain the project’s.

Yes, but not for anything essential: the app and its core features stay free. Whoever writes a plugin can sell it from their own store and the marketplace shows it with its price. The project charges authors no commission and never sees your payment details: you buy from the author's store, through a registered reseller.
Yes. The internet is only needed to download updates and new plugins. During an event Cuelith does not need it, not even for devices on the local network.

items.q: Can I use it for live streaming?
items.a: Not yet. Today Cuelith projects texts, songs and images on multiple screens. Camera, scenes and streaming are the next planned plugins.
It stays on your computer. Cuelith has no accounts and sends no personal data or content. It connects to the internet only to check for updates and read the list of plugins.

items.q: I already have my songs. Can I import them?
items.a: Yes, if they are in the open OpenLyrics or ChordPro formats, or as plain text. You can also export them all at once, as a backup.
Windows 10 or 11, or Linux, 64-bit. With one slide on air Cuelith uses about 600 MB of memory; each extra output adds about 120. The app itself shows you how much it is using.

items.q: Which languages is the app available in?
items.a: English and Italian, both included. At first launch Cuelith follows the language of your computer, and you can change it in Settings → General. More languages will arrive as plugins.

items.q: What happens if a plugin has a problem?
items.a: It is closed and restarted automatically, while the projection carries on. If it stops several times in a row it stays off and tells you. If the problem is in the plugin itself, support belongs to its author (you will find it on the plugin's page); to report it to the project, write from the Contact page.

items.q: How many plugins can I use together?
items.a: There is no fixed limit: every plugin runs in its own process, at a lower priority than the control view and the outputs. In our tests twelve light plugins take about 27 MB each and use nothing while idle; and with every core of the computer busy with plugins working flat out, the control view stays ready and the output smooth. The more plugins you switch on, the more powerful the computer needs to be: the indicator at the top tells you whether it copes, and if memory is about to run out Cuelith stops the heaviest plugin.

footer.privacy: The site uses no cookies and does not track visitors. Only the form to propose a plugin loads an anti-spam check from Cloudflare (Turnstile), which may store data in your browser.

support.title: Cuelith is free
support.text: No ads, no accounts. If it helps you, you can support its development with a small donation.
support.note: It is optional: Cuelith stays free for everyone.

how.title: How buying works
items: The plugin is sold by its author, from their own store at a registered reseller that handles payment, VAT and refunds. Cuelith does not collect any money and never sees your payment details.
The price you pay is the store's price: the project adds no commission.
After buying you receive a key by email. You enter it in Cuelith, on the plugin's card: it works on 3 computers at once and you can move it when you change computer.
If the store refunds you, the licence switches off by itself.

submit.title: Propose your plugin
submit.lead: One form, no account. The project reviews the plugin and, if everything is in order, publishes it in the Cuelith marketplace.

items.title: Write and package
items.text: Start from the plugin template and follow the developer guide. The package (.cpkg) must sit at a stable https address.

items.title: Fill in the form
items.text: Description, package, licence and, for a paid plugin, the details of your store.

items.title: We review
items.text: We check the package, the permissions, compatibility and the code of conduct. We reply to the address you give.

items.title: Publication
items.text: If the proposal is approved, the plugin appears in the marketplace on the website and inside Cuelith. Each new version is proposed again from the same form.

checklist.title: Conformity checklist
checklist.lead: To be published, the plugin must meet all of it: tick each item in the form.
checklist.paidTitle: In addition, for a paid plugin

items.noMalware: The plugin contains no malware, hidden code or undeclared data collection.
items.permissions: It declares in its manifest every permission it uses, and only those.
items.licence: It states its licence, proprietary ones (EULA) included, and where it can be read.
items.name: It does not use “Cuelith” in its own name (write “for Cuelith”) and does not copy code from the Cuelith core, which is GPL.
items.merchant: I sell it with my own store at Lemon Squeezy, which collects the payment, pays the VAT and handles refunds. The Cuelith project does not collect or touch my money.
items.devices: In the product I have turned on licence keys with a limit of 3 devices per key.
items.terms: I have read and accept the Conditions for publishing plugins in the marketplace and the privacy notice.
items.termsSpecific: I expressly approve, under articles 1341 and 1342 of the Italian Civil Code, the clauses in articles 2 (future changes), 5 (checks and responsibility), 6 (checking that the author is active), 8 (removal from the catalogue) and 11 (changes, law and jurisdiction).

paid.title: Paid plugins: how selling works
paid.intro: The marketplace sells nothing: it lists the plugin and sends people to your store. Today the registered reseller we support is Lemon Squeezy.
steps: Open your store and create the plugin's product, with licence keys and a limit of 3 devices per key.
Give the product's address below: it will be the “Buy” button in the catalogue and in the program. The project charges no commission.
Create your author key and sign every package: in the plugin template two commands are enough (pnpm keys, pnpm sign).
paid.refunds: You handle refunds from your store: a refund switches off the licence of the person who got it.
rules: Set the licence key to never expire if you sell the plugin once: the permission in Cuelith never outlasts the key's expiry, so a one-year key stops working after a year.
Each key works on 3 computers. Whoever changes computer deactivates the old one from the plugin (Plugins → Installed → “Deactivate this computer”) and activates the new one.
If a computer breaks and cannot be deactivated, free the seat yourself from your store (Lemon Squeezy: License keys → the key → activations): buyers must be able to contact you.
After a refund the key is deactivated and the plugin, at the next check, switches off outside live shows: nothing is ever stopped during a live show.

terms.title: Marketplace conditions
terms.intro: The full text is on the conditions page, which you accept by sending the proposal. In short:
items: Publishing is free: no commission, no exclusivity. You can sell the plugin elsewhere too.
The plugin follows the code of conduct (rights, no malware, honest data and permissions, compatibility) and passes the checks.
You give a real email address and keep it active: now and then we ask for a confirmation. With no reply the plugin may become “dormant” and we tell you.
If there is a problem we tell you and you have 14 days to fix it. People who already bought keep their licence if the plugin leaves the catalogue.

form.title: The form

id.label: Identifier
id.hint: In reverse-domain form, for example acme.lyrics-pro. Lowercase letters, numbers, dots and hyphens only. “cuelith” and “core” are reserved for the project.

description.label: Description
description.hint: What it does, in one or two sentences (10 to 300 characters).

publisher.label: Author or company
publisher.hint: The name shown on the card.

license.label: Plugin licence
license.hint: A licence name (for example MIT) or the name of your own terms of use (EULA).

eulaUrl.label: Where the licence or EULA can be read (optional)

packageUrl.label: Package address (.cpkg)
packageUrl.hint: https, stable and reachable by anyone. We check size, fingerprint and permissions. If the package has a cover image (the image field) and a first-use guide (the onboarding field), we show them on the plugin page.

repositoryUrl.label: Project page (optional)
repositoryUrl.hint: The plugin's website or repository, an https address.

authorKey.label: Author's public key
authorKey.hint: 43 characters. It signs your packages: required for a paid plugin, optional for a free one.

signature.label: Package signature
signature.hint: 86 characters, printed by “pnpm sign”. Required if you give the author's key.

price.label: Price to show
price.hint: Free text, for example “€9”. The real price is set in your store.

checkoutUrl.label: Purchase page of the product
checkoutUrl.hint: The product's address in your store (lemonsqueezy.com domain): it will be the “Buy” button.

storeId.label: Store number
storeId.hint: You can find it in your store settings.

productId.label: Product number
productId.hint: You can find it on the product page.

contact.label: Your email
contact.hint: Only used to reply to you. It is never published.

form.privacy: Your email is used to reply, for the periodic checks and for notices, and is never published. It is kept while the plugin is in the catalogue; rejected proposals are deleted. The form uses an anti-spam check from Cloudflare (Turnstile), which may store data in your browser.
form.needsScript: The form needs JavaScript to be turned on.

result.ok: Proposal received. We will reply to the address you gave.
result.unavailable: The service is not available right now. Please try again later.

errors.notHttps: The address must start with https://.

meta.title: Marketplace conditions · Cuelith
meta.description: The conditions for publishing a plugin, free or paid, in the Cuelith marketplace: free service, code of conduct, checks and removal.

sections.title: 1. The service
paragraphs: The marketplace is a free catalogue of plugins for Cuelith, run by the Cuelith project (the “Operator”). It offers a storefront and a simple way to install plugins from the program. The catalogue is in alphabetical order: there are no paid or featured positions.

The Operator does not sell plugins and is not a party to the sales contract. Paid plugins are sold by their author, from their own store at a registered reseller (today Lemon Squeezy), which collects the payment, pays the VAT and handles refunds.
These conditions do not change the GPL 3.0 licence of the program nor the exception for plugins.

sections.title: 2. Free and non-exclusive
paragraphs: Publishing in the marketplace is free: the Operator charges no commission and no fee.
The author may sell or distribute the plugin anywhere else, and may withdraw it from the catalogue at any time.

The Operator may introduce commissions or other economic conditions in the future. They apply only to plugins proposed after the change, or to plugins already listed if the author accepts them, and with 15 days' notice.

sections.title: 3. Who publishes and what they declare
paragraphs: Whoever proposes a plugin declares that they:
items: are the author of the plugin or have the right to distribute it under the licence they state;
state the licence, including a proprietary one, and where it can be read;
respect the licences of any third-party code they use;
give a real email address that they check and keep active while the plugin is in the catalogue;
say where users can get support.

sections.title: 4. Code of conduct
paragraphs: A plugin in the marketplace follows these rules, in letter and in spirit:
items: Rights. It does not infringe anyone's copyright, trademarks or other rights. It does not copy code from the Cuelith core, which is GPL. It does not use “Cuelith” in its own name: write “for Cuelith”.
No malware. It contains no malware, hidden or obfuscated code, nor functions the user cannot understand from the description.
Data. It does not collect, send or store user data without saying so clearly on its page and without the necessary permissions.
Honest permissions. It declares in the manifest all the permissions it uses, and only those.

Compatibility. It follows the technical rules published in the developer guide and passes the automatic compatibility checks. It does not interfere with what is on air: a plugin that hangs or answers too slowly is switched off, not the program.
Transparency. It shows the real price and where to buy. It does not mislead about its functions, name or author.
Lawful content. No illegal or discriminatory content, nor content that violates others' privacy.
Security. It fixes vulnerabilities in the plugin as soon as it knows of them and tells the Operator if they are serious.
Support. It answers the users of its own plugin: support belongs to the author, not to the project.

sections.title: 5. Checks and responsibility
paragraphs: The Operator runs automatic technical checks and a manual review of every proposal and every new version. They verify compatibility with Cuelith and compliance with these rules.
Passing the checks is not a guarantee: it does not ensure the absence of bugs, malware or infringements. The author is responsible for their plugin, its content and its support.
The Operator is not liable for damage caused by third-party plugins, within the limits of article 1229 of the Italian Civil Code (wilful misconduct and gross negligence remain excluded).

sections.title: 6. Checking that the author is active
paragraphs: To avoid leaving abandoned plugins in the catalogue, the Operator may periodically check that the package is still reachable and unchanged, and write to the author's address (about every 6 months) to ask for a one-click confirmation.

If the author does not reply, the request may be repeated twice more (three reminders in all). After the third reminder without a reply the plugin may become “dormant”: it can no longer be installed or bought from the catalogue, and the author receives a fourth, final message explaining what happened and how to fix it.
People who have already installed or bought the plugin keep using it and licences renew as before. The author can reactivate the plugin at any time by confirming they are there.

sections.title: 7. Reports
paragraphs: Anyone can report a problem with a plugin (malware, copyright infringement or anything else) by writing to {contact}.
The Operator notifies the author, who can reply, and then decides with a reasoned message. In case of malware or a serious breach the plugin is removed from the catalogue at once.

sections.title: 8. Removal from the catalogue
paragraphs: If a plugin does not comply with these conditions, the Operator tells the author the facts, at the email address given in the proposal form. The author has 14 days to fix it.
If not fixed, the plugin may be removed from the catalogue with a reasoned message. In serious cases (malware) removal is immediate.

Once removed, the plugin can no longer be installed or bought from the catalogue. Those who already installed or bought it keep it: licences already sold stay valid, renew and can be moved between computers. The Operator cannot uninstall a plugin from users' computers.

sections.title: 9. Complaints
paragraphs: The author can contest a decision by writing to {contact}. The Operator replies within 30 days.

sections.title: 10. Personal data
paragraphs: The author's email address is used to reply to the proposal, for the periodic checks, for notices and for reports. It is kept while the plugin is in the catalogue.

The Operator also keeps a record of the acceptance of these conditions (date, version, plugin identifier and email address) for 10 years after publication ends, as proof of the contract. The rest is in the privacy notice.

sections.title: 11. Changes, law and jurisdiction
paragraphs: The Operator may change these conditions with 15 days' notice, sent to the author's email address and by publishing the new version on this page.
Italian law applies. For disputes, the ordinary rules on jurisdiction apply.

sections.title: 12. Acceptance
paragraphs: Sending the proposal means accepting these conditions. The author also expressly approves, under articles 1341 and 1342 of the Italian Civil Code, the clauses in articles 2 (future changes), 5 (responsibility), 6 (checks and dormancy), 8 (removal) and 11 (changes, law and jurisdiction).
The technical rules for paid plugins (store, licence keys, 3 devices, signature) are on the “Propose a plugin” page.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lead: What data this site handles, why, for how long, and how you can exercise your rights.

meta.title: Privacy · Cuelith
meta.description: The privacy notice for the Cuelith site and marketplace.

sections.title: 1. Who handles the data
paragraphs: The data controller is the Cuelith project, run by a private individual. Contact: {contact}.

sections.title: 2. The site and the program
paragraphs: The site uses no cookies of its own, has no analytics tools and does not track visitors. The Cuelith program does not send usage data to the project.

sections.title: 3. People who propose a plugin
paragraphs: Data: plugin name, description, addresses, licence and contact email address. Purposes: assessing the proposal, communicating with the author, running the periodic checks, sending notices and handling reports and complaints. Legal basis: performance of the relationship with the author and legitimate interest in running a safe catalogue.

Retention: a pending proposal is deleted after 60 days; if rejected, at once. If approved, the email is kept while the plugin is in the catalogue. A record of the acceptance of the conditions (date, version, plugin identifier, email) is kept for 10 years after publication ends, as proof of the contract.
The plugin data (name, description, author, licence, addresses) is public in the catalogue. The email is not.

sections.title: 4. Anti-spam
paragraphs: The proposal form uses Cloudflare Turnstile, which may store information in your browser to tell a person from a program. It loads only on that page.
To limit submissions (5 a day) a fingerprint of the IP address, not the address, is kept for about 25 hours.

sections.title: 5. Licences for paid plugins
paragraphs: When a licence is activated, the program sends the “Notary” (a function of the site) the licence key, the plugin identifier and a public key generated by the computer. The Notary checks them with the reseller and replies. It does not store them.
The reseller (Lemon Squeezy) is an independent controller of the purchase data, which the project does not see.

sections.title: 6. Providers
paragraphs: The site and its functions are hosted by Cloudflare; the catalogue and the code by GitHub; payments are handled by the reseller. These providers may process data outside the European Union according to their own terms.

sections.title: 7. Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask for access to your data, rectification, erasure and restriction, and object to the processing, by writing to {contact}. Erasure may be limited for the record of acceptance, which serves as proof. You can also lodge a complaint with the Italian data protection authority.

sections.title: 8. Changes
paragraphs: If this notice changes, we publish the new version here, with the date.
